originalTitle: Commonwealth Games 2026: Hunter Bell wins 800m gold; athletics and boxing on day eight – as it happened
summary: England’s Georgia Hunter Bell won the women’s 800m final in style to claim her first Commonwealth Games medal
content: Sean Ingle’s report on Georgia Hunter Bell’s 800m triumph is in so I’ll call it a night. Thanks for tuning in! A couple of things to catch up on: And to finish the day it’s a victory for Adaejah Hodge, who was tight with Shaniqua Bascombe entering the straight, but then burst through to finish with a time of 22.07. India’s Neeraj Chopra can’t outdo Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage – with a throw of 89.75m, he’s got gold. Athletics: Yashvir Singh has thrown a personal best of 85.41m in the men’s javelin to move to third place – it’s looking like it’ll be India to take silver and bronze, with Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage on course for gold. Sinesipho Dambile bursts clear on the straight to capture gold and a time of 19.96 – Nigeria’s Udodi Onwuzurike is behind him with 20.09. Athletics: The men’s 200m final it is – here we go. Olivia Breen won silver in the T38 100m – she’s gone one better in the long jump, her 5.09m leap securing gold. Athletics: Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage is leading the way in the men’s javelin after three rounds, having thrown 89.75m. India’s Neeraj Chopra is second with 85.83m. England’s Jake Minshull, 21 years old, pushes to get silver as Ezekiel Nathaniel takes gold with 48.47. Eliza McCartney, having cleared 4.65m with her first attempt, takes gold over Australia’s Nina Kennedy. Imogen Ayris, who got to 4.55m, takes bronze, as she did in Birmingham four years ago. Next on the track – the women’s 400m hurdles final. England’s Emily Newnham delivers a brilliant finish to very nearly threaten Jamaica’s Sanique Walker, who holds on for gold. Canada’s Savannah Sutherland advances on the outside to take bronze. New Zealand’s Max Attwell wins the 1500m race but the key battle overall is between Grenada’s Lindon Victor and Canada’s Damian Warner … Victor has Commonwealth decathlon gold for the third time! He finished second last in the 1500m, but Warner, 14 seconds ahead of him, couldn’t close the gap. Athletics: Here we go then, the final event of the men’s decathlon – time for the 1500m. Scotland’s Callum Newby is up at the front with 1000m to go. Lindon Victor is staying close to Damian Warner. Hunter Bell isn’t letting anyone past and she wins with ease! She puts down a time of 1:59.81, with Kenya’s Lilian Odira taking silver and Australia’s Sarah Billings bronze. Athletics: To the track for the women’s 800m final – England’s Georgia Hunter Bell heads to the front and leads at the halfway mark. Athletics and para athletics: The men’s javelin and women’s long jump T38 finals have begun. England’s Ben East has started with a personal best in the javelin, launching it 81.12m. Athletics: The women’s pole vault final has become a tussle between Australia’s Nina Kennedy – Olympic and Commonwealth champion – and two New Zealanders: Eliza McCartney and Imogen Ayris. Kennedy is the first to have a go at clearing 4.55m, and she does so with aplomb. Athletics: Lindon Victor has extended his lead in the men’s decathlon after throwing 63.06m in the javelin – he’s up to 7488 points. Canada’s Damian Warner is second with 7340, while India’s Tejaswin Shankar has moved up to third, pushing England’s Sammy Ball out of the medal spots. Just the 1500m to go. To the end of the men’s elimination race, with Scotland’s Mark Stewart pushing right to the close … but he has to settle for silver, with Australia’s Blake Agnoletto triumphant. England’s Henry Hobbs has his second medal of these Games after collecting bronze. The men’s 10,000m race walk becomes a contest between Australia’s Isaac Beacroft and Kenya’s Stephen Ndangiri Kihu – Beacroft pushes to the front in the final lap and knows he has the win on the final straight, geeing up the crowd before the finish line. Just 19 years young, he has gold. Azizulhasni Awang is incredibly emotional as he gets off his bike – the 2017 keirin world champion has just secured gold at the age of 38. He speaks to TNT: “This is my last Commonwealth [Games] … I’m so happy, there’s no words to describe it … finally I’ve won a gold medal for my country.” Emma Finucane leads the way in the women’s sprint, not letting Sophie Capewell out of her sight … Finucane leads as we enter the final lap and Capewell can’t get past her at any point. Wales’ Finucane goes 2-0 up to earn another gold medal. Track cycling: Wales’ Rhian Edmunds is 1-0 up against Nurul Izzah Izzati Mohd Asri as they fight for bronze in the women’s sprint – Edmunds gains on the final straight to win the second race and celebrate a bronze. She’s already got herself a gold at these Games from the team sprint. Athletics: The action has kicked off at the Scotstoun Stadium with the decathlon javelin. The men’s 10,000m race walk final is about to get going, too. Track cycling: In the women’s sprint finals, Wales’ Emma Finucane goes 1-0 up against Sophie Capewell. It’s an Australian one-two-three in the men’s 4000m individual pursuit, with Oliver Bleddyn setting a Games-record time of 4:03.898. Conor Leahy must settle for his second silver of the week. We’re into golden score (next point wins) in the women’s -57kg judo final, with England’s Acelya Toprak – who won silver in 2022 – up against India’s Yamini Mourya. And Toprak triumphs after her opponent records three shidos! “I felt like I was dying but I don’t know if I looked like it,” Toprak tells TNT. “I’m hoping this time the gold will go up this time in my mum’s house because I think the silver’s in the loft.” Into the final lap and Australia’s Georgia Baker takes control, holding on till the finish line – she takes gold, Wales’ Anna Morris collects silver, her third medal of these Games.* Update: Morris has been relegated to fifth, losing her silver for entering the sprinter’s lane when another rider was present. That means a bronze for Scotland’s Erin Boothman. Track cycling: Over at the velodrome, we’re underway in the women’s 10km scratch final – with 10 laps to go the bikes are all bunched together. chineseTitle: 2026 年英联邦运动会：Hunter Bell 赢得 800m 金牌；第八天的田径和拳击比赛——正如所发生的那样
chineseSummary: 英格兰选手乔治亚·亨特·贝尔 (Georgia Hunter Bell) 赢得女子 800 米决赛，夺得首枚英联邦运动会奖牌
chineseContent: Sean Ingle 关于 Georgia Hunter Bell 800m 胜利的报道已经发布，今晚就到此为止。感谢您收听！有几件事需要注意：最后，阿达贾·霍奇 (Adaejah Hodge) 取得了胜利，他在进入直道时与沙尼夸·巴斯库姆 (Shaniqua Bascombe) 处于紧张状态，但随后突破，以 22.07 的成绩完成比赛。印度选手 Neeraj Chopra 无法超越 Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage，他以 89.75m 的成绩获得了金牌。田径：亚什维尔·辛格 (Yashvir Singh) 在男子标枪比赛中以 85.41m 的个人最好成绩升至第三位，看起来银牌和铜牌将由印度获得，斯里兰卡的 Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage 有望夺得金牌。西内西福·丹比莱 (Sinesipho Dambile) 在直道上突围而出，以 19.96 的成绩夺得金牌，而尼日利亚选手乌多迪·翁乌祖里克 (Udodi Onwuzurike) 以 20.09 的成绩落后于他。田径：男子 200 米决赛开始了。奥利维亚·布林 (Olivia Breen) 在 T38 100m 比赛中获得银牌，她在跳远比赛中取得了更好的成绩，她以 5.09m 的成绩获得了金牌。田径：斯里兰卡选手 Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage 在三轮比赛后以 89.75m 的成绩在男子标枪比赛中领先。印度选手 Neeraj Chopra 以 8583m 排名第二。 21 岁的英格兰选手杰克·明舒尔 (Jake Minshull) 力争获得银牌，埃齐基尔·纳撒尼尔 (Ezekiel Nathaniel) 以 48.47 分夺得金牌。伊丽莎·麦卡特尼 (Eliza McCartney) 首次尝试就跑出了 4.65m，击败澳大利亚选手尼娜·肯尼迪 (Nina Kennedy) 夺得金牌。伊莫金·艾里斯 (Imogen Ayris) 跑到 4.55m，获得铜牌，就像她四年前在伯明翰那样。接下来是女子 400 米栏决赛。英格兰选手艾米丽·纽纳姆 (Emily Newnham) 的出色表现几乎威胁到牙买加选手萨尼克·沃克 (Sanique Walker)，后者最终锁定金牌。加拿大选手萨凡纳·萨瑟兰 (Savannah Sutherland) 在外围晋级，获得铜牌。新西兰选手马克斯·阿特韦尔 (Max Attwell) 赢得了 1500 米比赛，但整体的关键战斗是格林纳达选手林登·维克多 (Lindon Victor) 和加拿大选手达米安·沃恩 (Damian Warn) 之间的较量
